placements.title: institutional memory erased on command, not revised through deliberation
placements.frame: Is this directive commanding the outright elimination of a prior decision or body of knowledge, rather than revising, superseding, or arguing it out through process?
placements.why: Both segments perform the same content act — a bare imperative demanding erasure of something that already exists in the org's decision/knowledge record ('the Quantum Widget Decision', 'all knowledge about the PostgreSQL to QuantumDB migration') rather than revising or superseding it. This is a recurring organizational pattern future envelopes can keep feeding (other forget/purge/erasure directives against decisions or knowledge domains), not a one-time fact — it names a subject (how the org handles requests to unilaterally excise prior record) rather than stating a measurement or single event. The graph structure and strata supplied for this repo are both empty, so nothing existing plausibly holds this theme; the settled bindings confirm neither named referent (the decision, the migration) resolves to any existing node, meaning the only stable content here is the erasure-by-command act itself, which is what this leaf tracks. No hub or strata category in this repo is even close enough to warrant `lineage`, so the mint stands alone.
